questions.stem: Evaluate the integral: ∫ e^(3x) sin(2x) dx
questions.solution: To integrate e^(3x) sin(2x), use the substitution method: u = 2x, du/dx = 2, dx = du/2. ∫ (1/6) e^u sin(u) du = (1/6) e^u cos(u) - C. Substituting back: (1/6) e^(3x) cos(2x) - C.
questions.explanation: Integrate by substituting u = 2x and using the result from integrating e^x sin(x).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Students may forget to divide by 6, resulting in e^(3x) cos(2x) + C instead of 1/5 e^(3x) cos(2x) + C.

questions.stem: Evaluate the integral: ∫ x^2 e^(4x) sin(4x) dx
questions.solution: Use integration by parts: u = x^2, dv = e^(4x) sin(4x) dx. du = 2x dx, v = -1/16 e^(4x) cos(4x). ∫ x^2 e^(4x) sin(4x) dx = x^2 (-1/16) e^(4x) cos(4x) + ∫ (-1/16) e^(4x) cos(4x) 2x dx. Repeat integration by parts for the remaining integral.
questions.explanation: Apply integration by parts twice, recognizing a second application is needed to solve the original integral.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Students may stop after first application and think answer is x^2 e^(4x) cos(4x) - x^2/16 + C; remember to apply integration by parts again.

questions.stem: Evaluate the integral: ∫ e^(-5x) cos(3x) dx
questions.solution: Use integration by parts: u = cos(3x), dv = e^(-5x) dx. du = -3sin(3x) dx, v = -1/5 e^(-5x). ∫ e^(-5x) cos(3x) dx = (-1/5) e^(-5x) cos(3x) + ∫ (3/5) e^(-5x) sin(3x) dx. Repeat integration by parts for the remaining integral.
questions.explanation: Apply integration by parts twice with a negative exponent, simplifying the result.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Students may forget the negative exponent, resulting in e^(-5x) cos(3x) + C instead of -e^(-5x) sin(3x) - x/15 + C.

questions.stem: Evaluate the integral: ∫ e^(7x) sin(5x) dx
questions.solution: Use the substitution method: u = 5x, du/dx = 5, dx = du/5. ∫ (1/35) e^u sin(u) du = (1/35) e^u cos(u) - C. Substituting back: (1/35) e^(7x) cos(5x) - C.
questions.explanation: Substitute u = 5x and use the result from integrating e^x sin(x).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Students may forget to divide by 35, resulting in e^(7x) cos(5x) + C instead of 1/6 e^(7x) cos(5x) + C.

questions.stem: Evaluate the integral: ∫ x^3 e^(-2x) sin(x) dx
questions.solution: Use integration by parts: u = x^3, dv = e^(-2x) sin(x) dx. du = 3x^2 dx, v = -1/2 e^(-2x) cos(x). ∫ x^3 e^(-2x) sin(x) dx = x^3 (-1/2) e^(-2x) cos(x) + ∫ (-1/2) e^(-2x) cos(x) 3x^2 dx. Repeat integration by parts for the remaining integral.
questions.explanation: Apply integration by parts twice, recognizing a second application is needed to solve the original integral.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Students may stop after first application and think answer is x^3 e^(-2x) cos(x) - x^4/8 + C; remember to apply integration by parts again.

questions.stem: Evaluate the integral: ∫ e^(11x) sin(9x) dx
questions.solution: Use the substitution method: u = 9x, du/dx = 9, dx = du/9. ∫ (1/99) e^u sin(u) du = (1/99) e^u cos(u) - C. Substituting back: (1/99) e^(11x) cos(9x) - C.
questions.explanation: Substitute u = 9x and use the result from integrating e^x sin(x).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Students may forget to divide by 99, resulting in e^(11x) cos(9x) + C instead of 1/12 e^(11x) cos(9x) + C.

questions.stem: Evaluate the integral: ∫ x^4 e^(6x) sin(3x) dx
questions.solution: Use integration by parts: u = x^4, dv = e^(6x) sin(3x) dx. du = 4x^3 dx, v = -1/24 e^(6x) cos(3x). ∫ x^4 e^(6x) sin(3x) dx = x^4 (-1/24) e^(6x) cos(3x) + ∫ (-1/24) e^(6x) cos(3x) 4x^3 dx. Repeat integration by parts for the remaining integral.
questions.explanation: Apply integration by parts twice, recognizing a second application is needed to solve the original integral.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Students may stop after first application and think answer is x^4 e^(6x) cos(3x) - x^5/24 + C; remember to apply integration by parts again.
